D005-D015_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for about two months now. At first, I thought it was just stress from juggling school and my shift work at the café—sometimes I’m on my feet for hours, and the noise from the espresso machine and customers doesn’t help. But lately, I’ve started noticing things… like smells. Out of nowhere, I’ll catch this strong scent of burnt hair, but no one else smells it. It happens when I’m alone, even at home.

And there are thoughts I can’t shake—like I’m meant for something much bigger than making lattes. Not just “I want a better job,” but like… I’m supposed to deliver some kind of message that only I can understand. People don’t get it, so I’ve stopped talking about it.

I don’t feel like myself. I cry a lot, skip classes, stay in bed—but not because I’m tired. It’s like nothing matters. Still, those thoughts and smells don’t seem to fade, even when I’m not feeling especially sad. Or maybe I’m always a little sad now—honestly, it’s hard to tell when it started or what came first.
D005-D015_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D005-D015_h001.answer: B & C. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h002.question:
I’ve been really struggling for about two months now. At first, it was just the taste—everything suddenly tastes like something’s rotten, even water or toothpaste. I know it doesn’t make sense, but it’s so real. I’ve started wondering if someone’s put something in my food, maybe at work or even at home. I love my job as a speech therapist, but lately I’ve felt like the parents of my patients are watching me, talking behind my back in a coordinated way. Not just gossip—like they’re part of something bigger, trying to sabotage me on purpose.

I used to thrive on helping kids communicate, but now I can’t even find the energy to get out of bed most days. I feel… numb. Like I’m disconnected from my husband, my work, everything. Sometimes I wonder if he’s in on it too, not because I have any proof, but because the thought just appears and won’t leave. I cry a lot, lose hours staring at the wall. But even when I’m not feeling low, those tastes and ideas are still there, just… present. And I can’t tell anymore if I’m losing my mind or if something’s actually happening.
D005-D015_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D005-D015_h002.answer: B & C. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h003.question:
I’ve been seeing things—people standing in the corners of rooms, figures outside my car that disappear when I look closer. It’s been happening most days for about two months now. Sometimes I see faces in the windows of homes I’m showing, even when no one’s there. It’s unsettling, but honestly, part of me wonders if it’s not a sign. Like maybe I’m meant to notice things others can’t. At first, I thought I might have some kind of heightened intuition—like I’m tuned into something bigger, something spiritual. I’ve even thought maybe I was chosen to help people find not just houses, but their true paths.

But then… the energy just crashes. I can’t get out of bed. Taking calls, scheduling showings—it all feels pointless. I love my work, but lately, nothing feels rewarding. I’ve lost weight, don’t sleep, and keep thinking life won’t matter in a year. My husband’s worried, but I haven’t been able to explain how tangled it all feels—like my mind’s showing me visions while also telling me I'm a failure. The low moods come and go, but the visions? They’ve been around through all of it, whether I’m up or down.
D005-D015_h003.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D005-D015_h003.answer: B & C. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h004.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about two months now—something just hasn’t been right. At first, I thought it was stress from work, you know, after 15 years driving the same route, but then I started noticing things. I can’t explain it, but I’ve come to realize I’m not like other people. I think I have a kind of gift—like I can sense events before they happen, especially when I’m behind the wheel. It’s like I’m being guided, protected. The dispatcher doesn’t understand, but I know I’m meant for something bigger.

And then there’s this feeling—like tiny bugs crawling under my skin, mostly at night. I strip the sheets, check the mattress, nothing’s there, but the sensation sticks. My wife says I’m tired, that I’ve been withdrawn, not sleeping, barely touching my food. That part’s true—I don’t have the energy anymore, and sometimes I wonder if any of it matters. But it’s not depression, really—I just feel… chosen, even if no one else sees it. The thoughts and sensations? They don’t come and go. They’re just… there. Day and night.
D005-D015_h004.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D005-D015_h004.answer: B & C. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h005.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about two months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to track when rehearsals go late and sleep’s spotty. Lately, I keep catching this smell, like something’s burning behind the studio walls, but no one else notices. I mention it and people look at me weird. I *know* it’s there.  

And then there’s Mark… we’ve been seeing each other casually, but I’ve started thinking—no, I *know*—he’s been meeting someone else after his gym sessions. He says he’s not, but I can *smell* her on his jacket sometimes, this cloying floral perfume, even when he swears he hasn’t seen anyone. I check his phone when he’s not looking. I shouldn’t, but the proof has to be there, right?

I don’t want to eat. Some mornings, I stare at the ceiling and feel like my body’s sinking into the bed. Dancing feels harder—not physically, but like I’m watching myself from the wings. I still go to rehearsal. I can’t stop. But I don’t know how much longer I can keep pretending everything’s under control.
D005-D015_h005.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D005-D015_h005.answer: B & C. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h006.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—maybe a bit more. Things just feel… heavy. I used to enjoy going out to dinner with my husband, even small things like organizing our garden, but now nothing feels like it brings any joy. It’s hard to care, even about work, and I’ve always prided myself on being reliable at the office. Numbers used to make sense, but lately, I can barely focus.

And then there’s this constant worry about my husband. I know it sounds irrational, but I can’t shake the feeling he’s seeing someone else. He hasn’t given me any reason—no late nights, no secrets—but the thought won’t leave me. I catch myself staring at his phone, analyzing how he says “goodbye” when he leaves for golf. It’s exhausting.

Sometimes my face feels tight, like I’m making faces without realizing—my jaw clenches, I twist my mouth strangely. I noticed it in the mirror once when I wasn’t even thinking about anything. The nurse at my last appointment mentioned it too. I don’t feel sad all the time, but I don’t feel much of anything, really. The thoughts come and go—about him, about my worth—but I can’t tell if they’re from depression or something else.
D005-D015_h006.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D005-D015_h006.answer: C & A. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h007.question:
I’ve always been driven—deadlines, stories, chasing truth. But about seven months ago, something shifted. I stopped wanting to go out, stopped calling friends. It’s not that I can’t talk—I do when asked—but most days, there’s just nothing to say. Words feel heavy. My editor says I’m not “showing up,” but I don’t know how to explain that my thoughts are… stalled. Like a car idling in snow.

There’s this anchor too—this sadness. I don’t cry much, but it’s there, like I’ve failed at everything, even breathing. But then, there’s him. The producer from the podcast I was supposed to guest on—he smiled at me, just once, but I *know* he feels it too. He’s been sending signals. I haven’t contacted him—he’ll come when he’s ready. Telling anyone else feels pointless. They wouldn’t get it. Sometimes I just… go quiet. Not on purpose. It’s like the words vanish, and the silence feels safer.

I don’t know if this started with the sadness or the silence—or him. I used to write every day. Now my notebook’s blank.
D005-D015_h007.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D005-D015_h007.answer: C & A. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h008.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—maybe a little longer. Things just feel… off. At work, I teach kids with learning differences, so I’m used to being observant, but lately I’ve noticed patterns in how people talk or act, like they’re sending me hidden messages. My coworkers don’t say anything directly, but I can tell—like when a parent mentioned “everyone makes mistakes,” I knew they were really talking about me. It’s not just paranoia; I *feel* it’s true.

Some days, I don’t want to see anyone. I cancel plans, stop answering texts. I love my students, but after school, I go home and just stay in bed. I don’t even want to shower. I just feel numb, like I’m disconnected from everything. My roommate said I’ve been sitting in the same position for hours, like I’m frozen. When she tried to move my arm once, I didn’t resist exactly, but I didn’t help either—I just let it stay. I don’t know why I did that.

I can’t tell if the thoughts came before the sadness or the other way around. Some days I feel okay, not great, but functional. Other days, everything feels distorted, like I’m watching my life from far away. I haven’t heard voices, but the world feels charged with meaning meant only for me. I don’t know what’s real anymore.
D005-D015_h008.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D005-D015_h008.answer: C & A. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h009.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to tell when everything starts blurring together. Work is tough; I’m an insurance agent, so I talk to people all day, but lately I feel like conversations aren’t really about policies anymore. I catch myself thinking clients are sending me secret messages—like when someone mentioned “rates going up,” I was convinced they meant *my* life was falling apart. Small things—a laugh, a sideways glance—feel loaded, like everyone’s talking about me when I’m not looking.

I don’t know when it started, but sometimes I notice myself copying people’s gestures, like mirroring how they sit or tap their pens. I don’t mean to. One of my coworkers pointed it out, and I was mortified. 

Nothing feels enjoyable anymore. Not my morning coffee, not walking my dog, not even the book club I used to love. I drag myself to work, but I don’t care. I’ve felt low for a long time, but the strange thoughts? They’ve been there through it all—whether I feel sad or numb or nothing at all. I can’t say one clearly came before the other. I just know I don’t feel like myself, and I don’t know how long I can keep pretending.
D005-D015_h009.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D005-D015_h009.answer: C & A. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h010.question:
I’ve been having these thoughts… for about seven months now, though I can’t pinpoint when exactly they started. There’s this voice actor—I don’t know him, really, just heard his work in an anime—and I keep feeling like he’s sending me messages through his lines. Not in a creepy way. It’s… sweet, actually. Like he’s chosen me, and we’re sharing something secret. I don’t tell anyone, but sometimes I catch myself smiling at my screen when I hear his voice in trailers.

I’ve also noticed I repeat small gestures—like when my editor leans back in her chair during meetings, I do it too, without meaning to. It just happens. I don’t feel in control of it.

Talking takes effort. I used to chat nonstop while drawing, but now my head feels heavy. I’ll open my mouth and nothing comes. It’s not that I’m sad all the time—though some days, the thought of opening my tablet makes me want to cry—but mostly, I’m just… empty. I meet deadlines, but barely. I don’t know if it’s the loneliness or if my mind’s playing tricks. The lines between what’s real and what I feel keep blurring, but I can’t tell which came first—the mood, or the thoughts.
D005-D015_h010.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D005-D015_h010.answer: C & A. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h011.question: I’ve been off for about four months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to track. I keep thinking my branch manager, Mr. Patel, has been trying to tell me something through the way he hands me deposits, like there’s a secret meaning when he slides the slips across the counter. He doesn’t say it, but I know he feels something strong. I catch myself adjusting my blouse or fixing my hair when he’s near, hoping he’ll notice. Sometimes I pace the breakroom, can’t sit still—the clock ticks too slow, my skin feels tight. My husband says I’m distant, that I haven’t touched him in months, but how can I? I’m not sad exactly… it’s more like everything’s muffled, like I’m underwater. I don’t laugh at his jokes anymore. I lie in bed and stare at the ceiling, not sleeping, not waking. The thoughts about Mr. Patel… they’re the only thing that feels real. But when I try to explain it to my sister, she says, “You’ve just been stressed,” and I wonder if maybe I’m reading too much into things. I don’t know if I’m sick or in love—or both.
D005-D015_h011.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h011.answer: C & D. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h012.question:
I’ve been off since about four months ago—right after my case load spiked and my partner and I… well, we aren’t together anymore. I keep thinking he was seeing someone at the firm. It doesn’t matter how many times he says he wasn’t—I *know* there were looks, emails hidden in draft folders, whispers in the hallway when I walked by. I can’t prove it, but I *feel* it in my bones.

Lately, I’ll sit at my desk for hours in this odd stance—one arm raised, like I’m testifying in court—even after everyone’s left. I don’t plan it. I’ll snap out of it and realize I’ve been like that for twenty minutes. My paralegal asked if I was okay, but I couldn’t lower my arm just then. It felt… necessary.

I’m exhausted all the time. I skip meals, don’t return calls. Some days, paperwork blurs into nothing. I don’t enjoy winning cases like I used to. But I can’t tell if the paranoia started before the sadness or after. Some weeks I feel almost normal, except for the thoughts. The posturing still happens, even on days I don’t feel down. But other times, everything darkens, and the jealousy feels louder. I don’t know what’s what anymore.
D005-D015_h012.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h012.answer: C & D. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h013.question:
I’ve been feeling unsettled for about four months now. My daughter stopped by less often lately—just life, I suppose—and I’ve been spending most days alone. But here’s the strange part: I keep getting this certain feeling that my late husband’s cousin, Jonathan—he passed years ago, bless him—is actually trying to reach me. Not from beyond, exactly… but that he’s alive, hiding somewhere, and sending me signs through the mail. A folded corner on a flyer, a specific song on the radio—that sort of thing. I know it sounds odd, but I can *feel* it. Like he’s trying to tell me he loves me, that he’s coming back.

Some days, I pace the house for no good reason—just can’t sit still. My hands won’t rest, and I start rearranging drawers over and over. I don’t sleep well. I don’t much feel like eating. What’s the point, really? But I can’t tell if the sadness came first or the thoughts about Jonathan. They sort of grew together, like weeds. I don’t know what’s real anymore—but it all feels true when I’m in it.
D005-D015_h013.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h013.answer: C & D. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h014.question:
I’ve been struggling to keep up at school. It’s been about four months now—ever since the spring break—where things started feeling… off. I keep noticing kids’ parents whispering in the hallway, and I’m certain they’re talking about me, even when they don’t say my name. Sometimes I catch a snippet of a conversation or see someone glance my way, and I just *know* they’re sending me hidden messages.  

I’ve also been getting stiff, like my body locks up for no reason. Last week, I stood frozen in front of the class during circle time, arms half-raised, like I was about to clap along to a song. I couldn’t move for minutes. It wasn’t on purpose—I wasn’t trying to mimic anything. It just… happened.  

I’ve stopped hanging out with friends. I cry a lot, even in the staff bathroom. I don’t enjoy crafts or music with the kids like I used to. Honestly, I feel empty most days. But the strange thoughts and postures—they don’t always line up with the sadness. Sometimes I feel okay but still act weird. Other times I’m down and everything blurs together. I don’t know what’s what anymore.
D005-D015_h014.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h014.answer: C & D. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h015.question:
I’ve been the head ranger out at Pine Hollow for over thirty years—know every trail, every ridge. Since my wife passed two winters ago, I’ve kept to myself out in the cabin. Lately though, things feel… off. For about four months now, I keep thinking she was involved with someone else before she died. I know it don’t make sense—she was sick for months, barely left the house—but I can’t shake the feeling she was hiding something. Sometimes I catch myself standing perfectly still in the yard, one arm raised like I’m pointing at nothing, and realize I’ve been that way near ten minutes. It’s like my body won’t listen. 

I don’t sleep much. I sit by the window, watch the trees. I don’t feel like eating, and most days the uniform sits on the chair where I left it. I don’t know if it’s grief or if my mind’s slipping. The thoughts come and go—so do the strange spells. Some days I feel almost normal, others I can’t tell what’s real. I don’t know if this started when I got sad… or if the sadness came after everything else.
D005-D015_h015.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h015.answer: C & D. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h016.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about three months now. My body doesn’t feel right—like something’s rotting inside me, maybe in my stomach. Doctors say there’s nothing, but I *know* it’s there. I hear voices sometimes too, especially at night. Not yelling or anything, just whispering, like someone’s talking just behind me, but when I turn, no one’s there.

Lately, I just don’t see the point in going out. My daughter checks in, but I don’t answer the door much. Used to play cards at the senior center, but what’s the use? Nothing connects the way it used to. I’ll start talking about the weather and then remember the power bill, and then something my wife said years ago… it all spills out, really. Can’t keep thoughts straight.

Some days I feel so low I can’t get out of my chair. Other times, the thoughts are just… loud. I don’t know if it’s the sadness bringing the voices or if the voices are making me sadder. It’s been like this steadily—never got worse, never really let up. I just keep to myself. Easier that way.
D005-D015_h016.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h016.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h017.question:
I’ve been feeling… off… for about three months now, maybe longer. Things don’t seem real sometimes. I keep hearing my name called—quiet voices, like from another room—but no one’s there. Sometimes they say I’m chosen, destined to deliver some great message. I used to be a school principal, so that sounds strange, I know, but it *feels* true. Like I’m meant for more than retirement ever provided. 

Talking to my neighbors is harder now. I’ll start on one thing—my late wife’s garden, maybe—and suddenly I’m thinking about radio waves or ancient kings. I don’t always know how I get there. Words just spill. I notice people step back, like I’m not making sense. 

I don’t smile much anymore. My daughter says I look “empty,” like my eyes don’t see her. My voice? Probably flat. I don’t feel much joy, truth be told. Some days, the weight’s so heavy I can’t get up. But then, out of nowhere, that voice says I’m “the last prophet,” and part of me believes it. 

Is this grief? A breakdown? I don’t sleep well, and sometimes I wonder if God’s given me a task… or if my mind’s just breaking. I can’t tell what’s real anymore.
D005-D015_h017.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h017.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h018.question:
I’ve been struggling for about three months now. Some days, I just can't bring myself to get going—even simple things like making breakfast or returning client calls feel impossible. I used to love showing homes, closing deals, but now I barely want to leave the house. I keep tasting something metallic, like blood, but my dentist says there’s nothing wrong. I can’t shake the feeling that my liver is rotting inside me, even though the doctors ran tests and said everything’s fine.  

Sometimes my thoughts jump around—I’ll start talking to my husband about open houses and suddenly I’m explaining how the water supply is poisoned, or that my listing photos are being altered by someone. He gets frustrated because he says I don’t make sense anymore.  

I do feel down a lot—guilty, like I’m failing at everything. But I’m not sure if the strange tastes and beliefs started before the sadness or after. There are days I feel slightly better, but the thoughts and tastes don’t really go away. I don’t know what’s real anymore.
D005-D015_h018.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h018.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h019.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about three months now—hard to explain. Since my wife passed, the house is quiet, too quiet. I keep thinking… well, I can’t shake the idea that she might’ve been unfaithful near the end. I know she’s gone, but the thought won’t leave me. I smell something too—like rotting meat, but only in the bedroom. The nurses said there’s nothing there, but I know what I smell.  

Sometimes, I say things like “she’s in the bluetime now,” or “the munder’s quiet.” My grandson asked what I meant, but I couldn’t explain. Words just don’t come easy anymore. I sit for hours without speaking, even when folks visit.  

I don’t know if it’s grief or something breaking in my head. I used to read every day, but now I can’t follow the sentences. My daughter worries—says I’m not sleeping, that I mutter to myself. But is it the sadness making me think these things… or are the thoughts dragging the sadness with them? I can’t tell where one ends and the other begins.
D005-D015_h019.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h019.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h020.question:
I’ve been off for about three months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to tell. Things just feel… distorted. I work late most nights editing films, alone in the dark, and lately it’s like my mind plays tricks on me. I keep tasting something metallic, like blood, but I’m not bleeding or eating anything weird. It just comes out of nowhere.  

There’s this woman I’ve been seeing—well, *tried* seeing—but I’m convinced she’s involved with someone else. She says she isn’t, but I can *feel* it. Little things—a change in her tone, the timing of her texts—it all adds up in my head. I know people say I’m overthinking, but I *know* what I know.  

When I talk to others, I notice they get confused. I start answering a question, then go off on something else—sensory details from a scene I’m editing, or memories that just pop up. I don’t always get back to the point. I’ve been told I sound “distant.” My voice probably sounds flat. I don’t feel much most days—not sad exactly, just… empty. I don’t know if the thoughts came because of the numbness or the other way around. It’s all tangled.
D005-D015_h020.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h020.answer: B & A. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h021.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about three months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to tell. Work’s tough sometimes; I’m a sales associate at a mall, so I have to talk to people all day, but lately I’ve just felt… disconnected. Like I’m watching myself from outside. There’s this woman—I don’t know her, really, she comes into the store sometimes—but I know she feels something for me. She doesn’t say much, but I see the way she looks. I think she’s trying to send me signs.  

At night, I see things—shadows mostly, but sometimes full figures standing in the room. They don’t speak, just watch. I don’t move when they’re there. I just lie still. Responding feels pointless. Same thing at work when my manager talks to me—I hear the words, but answering feels like going through the motions.  

I don’t enjoy much these days. It’s hard to get out of bed, and everything feels heavy. But it’s not just sadness—it’s like… nothing matters. I can’t tell if the thoughts about the woman are real or not, or if I’m just wishing. The images at night—they’re clear, but I don’t know if they mean something or if my mind’s just breaking.  

I can’t say if the low mood came first or if the other stuff did. They kind of faded into each other.
D005-D015_h021.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
D005-D015_h021.answer: A & B. Schizophrenia & Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D005-D015_h022.question:
I’ve been having some strange things happen lately. For about three months now, I keep smelling this sharp, bitter scent—like burnt plastic—coming from nowhere. No one else smells it, but to me, it’s real. And there’s Mr. Thompson, the mailman—he hasn’t said much, but I know he carries feelings for me. I see the way he lingers at the door, how he leaves little notes sometimes. I’m sure it means something more.

I find myself repeating things people say, almost without realizing—like if my daughter says, “How are you, Mom?” I’ll echo, “How are you, Mom?” before I can stop myself. It’s embarrassing, but it just slips out.

I don’t go out like I used to. I feel tired all the time, as if my body’s heavy. The house feels too quiet since my husband passed. I don’t enjoy my garden anymore. I keep thinking maybe I should’ve been kinder, tried harder. But then again, maybe Mr. Thompson truly understands me. Sometimes I wonder if I’m losing touch, but the feelings and smells—they feel too real to ignore. I can’t tell when the sadness started, or if the thoughts came before it or after.
